task: Apply proposed_fix_sketch item 1 from decode-compiler-tree-lexer-rebuild-cost-finding.json: cache a built Lark Lexer/Scanner per grammar alongside _load_parser's cached Lark object, have _lex_tokens reuse it instead of self._parser.lex(prefix); confirm compiler-side call counts / wall time drop with zero change to n_paths/coverage.

summary: New _load_lexer(grammar_path) @lru_cache(maxsize=4) alongside _load_parser; calls _load_parser(grammar_path)._build_lexer() once per grammar path (the same construction Lark.lex() performs internally, now cached).

New _lex(text) helper: LexerThread.from_text(self._lexer, text).lex(None); _lex_tokens (called by every _sync via _full_sync/_incremental_sync) now calls self._lex(...) instead of self._parser.lex(...).
No change to _full_sync/_incremental_sync/_sync control flow, InteractiveParser feed loop, or grammar/terminal definitions -- only which lexer object performs tokenization.
change.why_safe: Lark.lex(text) with parser='lalr' always takes the uncached _build_lexer(dont_ignore) branch (self.lexer is never set for that parser mode) -- a fresh BasicLexer from the same LexerConf every call. _load_lexer calls that identical _build_lexer() method once and caches the result; BasicLexer already lazily caches its own Scanner (self._scanner) once built, so reusing the BasicLexer object reuses that existing lazy cache instead of discarding it every call. Verified list(parser.lex(prefix)) == list(LexerThread.from_text(parser.parser.lexer, prefix).lex(None)) directly.

interpretation: Confirms the finding's root-cause chain and closes proposed_fix_sketch item 1. The Lark grammar object was already cached (_load_parser); the lexer/scanner built from it was not. Caching it removes the rebuild (thousands-of-calls-per-query -> 0 after process warm-up) without touching tokenization semantics, since the cached BasicLexer is constructed from the identical LexerConf the uncached path would have used.
scope_note: No train/eval run, no checkpoint, no --ship-gates scoreboard -- harness-internal correctness+perf fix with unit-test coverage, not a readiness claim. The ~2-2.1x wall-time win is on build_completion_forest micro-calls in isolation, not re-measured against full per-record compiler_ms telemetry or the exposure12 eval protocol. _incremental_sync still re-lexes the entire current prefix on every call (proposed_fix_sketch item 2, not applied this session) -- only lexer *construction* is cached, not made incremental at the token-stream level.
